newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: KYRGYZSTAN SEES 1.60-1.65 MLN TONNE GRAIN HARVEST.
newsitem.headline: KYRGYZSTAN SEES 1.60-1.65 MLN TONNE GRAIN HARVEST.

text.p: Kyrgyzstan aims to boost gross grain production to a record 1.60 to 1.65 million tonnes in 1997 from 1.49 million in 1996, Agriculture Minister Zhumakadyr Akeneyev said on Monday.

"This year Kyrsyzstan plans to gather a record grain crop," Akeneyev told a news briefing. "The harvest campaign this year started two weeks earlier than last year, and is going strictly according to schedule."
The Central Asian republic's grain needs are around 850,000 tonnes a year, and it is looking for new grain export markets this season, he said.
The minister said Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan were also looking forward to good harvests this year, adding that Turkmenistan could well be a buyer of Kyrgyz grain.
Akeneyev said the 1997 grain campaign in the former Soviet state was going ahead as planned, with 53.2 percent of the area sown to grain harvested by August 8.
Yields per hectare up to that date had averaged at 2.53 tonnes compared with 2.36 tonnes in 1996.
The agriculture ministry was planning to set up a major storage facility for this year's crop, and would buy grain harvested by farmers.
Kyrgyzstan also hoped to develop its food processing industry in 1997, using South Korean credits worth about $16 million.
"This year we will fully secure our own basic food product needs," Akeneyev said.
